title: BNCI 2019-001 Motor Imagery dataset for Spinal Cord Injury patients
description: EEG recordings from 10 persons with cervical spinal cord injury performing attempted arm and hand movements: hand open, palmar grasp, lateral grasp, pronation and supination. Sixty-one EEG channels and 3 EOG channels were recorded at 256 Hz across 9 runs, giving 360 trials per participant. The data show that movement-related cortical potentials in low-frequency EEG can be decoded offline in five classes. They also support an online proof-of-concept for self-paced movement detection, relevant to neuroprosthetic control.
methods_description: Participants attempted or executed movements according to visual cues while fixating on a cross. EEG was recorded with g.tec active electrodes (61 channels, 10-5 montage, left earlobe reference) plus 3 EOG channels at 256 Hz, with a 0.01-100 Hz bandpass and a 50 Hz notch filter. Each participant completed 9 runs of 72 trials per class in total. Preprocessing included ICA-based artifact removal, and classification used shrinkage LDA on 0.3-3 Hz low-frequency signals.
